artifacts.summary: Four-phase sequential implementation plan applying Route 3 (Quotient.recOnSubsingleton) to make the four LJ/LK context-based Decidable instances computable, with executable conformance tests and an axiom-census re-baseline

memory_candidates.content: To make a Decidable instance over a Finset-indexed proposition computable when the natural encoding is order-dependent (so no computable Finset -> value function exists), eliminate from the underlying Multiset quotient directly into the Decidable, using Quotient.recOnSubsingleton on `s.val` with motive `fun (m : Multiset a) => (h : m.Nodup) -> Decidable (P (Finset.mk m h))`, applied to `s.nodup`. This is legitimate because Decidable p is a Subsingleton: the DECISION is representative-independent even when the intermediate encoding is not. Structure eta makes `Finset.mk s.val s.nodup` definitionally `s`, so no cast or rewrite is needed at the instance level. Mathlib precedents: Multiset.decidableMem (Data/Multiset/Defs.lean) and Finset.Nontrivial.instDecidablePred (Data/Finset/Insert.lean). Two traps: (1) the list-level worker MUST be a separate named def -- fully inlining it into the recursor's lambda fails to elaborate, because the representative appears as the quotient form rather than the coercion, so a toFinset rewrite finds no occurrence; the named form works because the coercion resolves by unification against the helper's declared type. (2) This route avoids adding a [LinearOrder a] hypothesis that a Finset.sort-based approach would force onto every public instance.
